newsitem.title: RUSSIA: South Russian leader wants to legalise blood feuds.
newsitem.headline: South Russian leader wants to legalise blood feuds.

text.p: The president of a southern Russian republic has proposed legalising the tradition of blood feuds by which the relatives of a murder victim avenge his death by killing the murderer, Russian television said on Tuesday.

"The blood feud exists all over Ingushetia. All over Ingushetia. If a person kills somebody, he will definitely be killed, too. Surely this should be enshrined in law," said Ruslan Aushev, President of Ingushetia in the North Caucasus.
"Why should we not legalise it? We must allow the republics which have such customs and traditions to introduce a legal framework for the blood feud," Aushev added in remarks broadcast on television.

Despite efforts by former Soviet leaders to stamp them out, blood feuds continue in several of the southern republics in the vast Russian Federation, whose multi-ethnic, 150 million-strong population is almost all governed by a single criminal code.

An exception is Chechnya, the republic neighbouring Ingushetia, where Moslem separatist leaders have introduced elements of Islamic Sharia law since a 21-month conflict with Russian troops ended last year.
